paper.central_claim: SWE-Exp: distilling a multi-faceted experience bank (comprehension perspectives/reflections and modification strategies) from prior successful and failed repair trajectories, retrieving and adapting one relevant experience per decision point inside an MCTS Instructor/Assistant agent, lifts SWE-Bench Verified Pass@1 to 73.0% (Claude 4 Sonnet) and 42.0% (DeepSeek-V3), moving agents from memoryless exploration to experience-driven repair.
paper.title: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution

reason: Full text and appendices read. A non-weight experience bank (distilled text from past trajectories) is written offline and read at later issues; in scope as system_method. Bank is built in one offline pass from baseline trajectories, with no update/forgetting/gating loop.

evidence.quote: However, current agents act as memoryless explorers—treating each problem separately without retaining or reusing knowledge from previous repair experiences.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: the fixed thing is per-issue statelessness.

evidence.quote: An Experiencer agent is instructed to extract experiences from both success and failure trajectories.
evidence.support_explanation: Write path: LLM reflector over both outcomes.

evidence.quote: disables cross-repository experience abstraction and instead directly uses the raw problem statement and golden patch as in-context demonstrations
evidence.support_explanation: Shows golden patches are available to extraction / raw-demo baseline; alternative-abstraction control exists.

evidence.quote: To prevent data leakage, we exclude all experiences originating from the same code repository and generated after the target instance.
evidence.support_explanation: Leakage guard: same-repo later experiences removed; same-repo earlier ones remain allowed.

evidence.quote: During the experience collection phase, we run SWE-Search on the SWE-Bench-Verified benchmark, collect the resulting trajectories, and extract structured experiences from them.
evidence.support_explanation: Bank is built offline once from the baseline's own trajectories on the evaluation benchmark; not an iterative loop of SWE-Exp's own runs.
Headline: +6.6 pt (DeepSeek), +2.2 pt (Claude) over SWE-Search; one run, 500 instances.

evidence.quote: SWE-Exp 42.0% - w/o Comprehension Experience 38.8% -3.2% w/o Modification Experience 39.4% -2.6% w/o Dual-Agent 39.8% -2.2% w/o Experiences Extraction 36.0% -6.0% w/o LLM Reranking 38.2% -3.8%
evidence.support_explanation: Component ablations (DeepSeek only); raw-demo variant (36.0) is below the no-experience level (37.8, E009).

evidence.quote: Without any experience, the system achieves 37.8% Pass@1. The performance peaks at 42.0% when exactly 1 experience is used, while dropping as the number continues to increase.
evidence.support_explanation: Store-off control inside the full scaffold: +4.2 pt; k chosen at the peak on the same 500 instances.

evidence.quote: While a single experience boosted Pass@1 from 37.2% to 42.0%, adding more examples degraded performance, dropping to 39.8% with two experiences and further declining to 39.0% with four experiences.
evidence.support_explanation: Internal inconsistency: no-experience baseline reported as 37.2% here and 37.8% in 5.3; non-monotone k curve.

evidence.quote: a dedicated reranking agent evaluates these candidates and selects
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval is N=10 by cosine on issue type/description, LLM rerank to k=1.

evidence.quote: its training data composition is not publicly disclosed, making it impossible to verify potential overlap with our evaluation dataset
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede base-model contamination cannot be excluded.

evidence.quote: the average token consumption increases only slightly (203.3K vs. 189.1K), while the average API usage cost remains nearly unchanged ($0.13 vs. $0.12)
evidence.support_explanation: Per-instance online overhead vs SWE-Search (DeepSeek); bank-construction cost absent.

evidence.quote: Moreover, the agent currently lacks a robust mechanism to assess the applicability of prior experiences in novel contexts, which may lead to inappropriate reuse or misleading to irrelevant patterns.
evidence.support_explanation: No applicability gate or maintenance of reused experience.

evidence.quote: While SAGE emphasizes stage-wise self-improvement within a single repair process, its experience is primarily localized to the current instance.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' differentiation from the nearest experience-driven neighbor.

evidence.quote: a large number of issues (131) are consistently resolved across all settings.
evidence.support_explanation: Instance-level variability across experience settings is substantial; evidence that single-run margins of a few points are noise-prone.

evidence.quote: consisting of 25 issues each from Django, SymPy, and Sphinx
evidence.support_explanation: Bank-size analysis uses a 75-instance subset on DeepSeek only.

evidence.quote: We manually verified the correctness of LLM-extracted experiences on a subset of 75 instances
evidence.support_explanation: Extraction quality only spot-checked on 75 instances, no reported error rate.

evidence.quote: Compared to SAGE and EvoCoder, two other experience-driven frameworks that also build upon SWE-Bench-verified trajectories, SWE-Exp attains a higher resolution rate under identical model conditions.
evidence.support_explanation: Neighbor comparison is by table numbers; provenance (rerun vs copied) of baseline numbers not stated.

signatures.object: Experience Bank: vector DB of LLM-distilled text items (comprehension perspective / failure reflections; modification strategies) indexed by LLM-generated issue_type and description
signatures.information: Past SWE-Search trajectories on SWE-Bench-Verified labeled success/failure by ground-truth tests; Experiencer also sees the golden patch; target instance's own patch/trajectory not visible (same-repo later instances excluded)
signatures.operation: Experiencer abstracts perspective (success) or reflections vs golden patch (failure) and up to 3 modification insights; embed; at test time retrieve N=10 by cosine, LLM rerank to k=1, Reuser rewrites experience for the issue / rewrites the Instructor's instruction
signatures.output: Guidance text injected into Instructor (comprehension) and Assistant instruction (modification)
signatures.conditions: Ground-truth success labels and golden patches available for past issues; embeddings of issue type/description
signatures.feedback: Test-validated resolution outcome and golden patch of earlier issues
signatures.selection_rule/data: No admission gate beyond outcome annotation; all items stored; one item retrieved per decision by rerank
signatures.persistence: Offline-built bank, frozen during evaluation; per-instance membership varies by repo/time exclusion; no update, merge, expiry or rollback
signatures.later_use: Retrieved at each MCTS decision node of later issues
signatures.failure_boundary: Misleading experience (k>1 degrades), no applicability check, bank construction uses privileged supervision, single benchmark/language

signatures.object: Instructor/Assistant dual-agent role split inside MCTS
signatures.operation: Instructor issues next-step instruction, Assistant executes tool action
signatures.selection_rule/data: not_applicable: static architecture, no feedback-driven selection or retention
signatures.failure_boundary: Confound with experience gain in headline comparison to SWE-Search

gap.author_gap: SWE agents treat each issue in isolation (redundant exploration, no knowledge transfer, no strategic evolution) and prior experience frameworks are general-purpose, lacking software-engineering-specific structure.
gap.checked_gap: The statelessness limitation is real and the neighbors (ExpeL, AutoGuide, AgentRR, EvoCoder, SAGE, ExACT) are named and two are compared; the SE-specific residual is cross-repository, two-facet abstraction, argued qualitatively against SAGE's within-instance abstractions. Evidence for redundant exploration across similar issues is by citation, not measured here.
gap.lineage/closest_adjacent: ExpeL (insight store with ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE), EvoCoder (reflection for issue reproduction), SAGE (plan abstractions from own task experience), AutoGuide, AgentRR, ExACT; base scaffold SWE-Search (MCTS).
gap.residue: Reuse across heterogeneous repositories; noise from multiple retrieved experiences; applicability assessment of retrieved experience.
gap.stakes: Resolution rate on SWE-Bench Verified and wasted search effort.
gap.method_response: Offline distillation into comprehension/modification facets, similarity retrieval + LLM rerank, k=1 adaptation by Reuser, role-split agents.
gap.remaining_gap: No maintenance/gating of the bank, no applicability scoring (authors), no online accumulation loop, no multi-language evidence.
unresolved: Neighbor papers (ExpeL, SAGE, EvoCoder) not in pinned materials: provenance and comparability of their table numbers cannot be verified

claims.text: SWE-Exp achieves 73.0% (Claude 4 Sonnet) and 42.0% (DeepSeek-V3) Pass@1, outperforming other agent frameworks.
claims.setting: SWE-Bench Verified, 500 issues, SWE-Search scaffold extended
claims.baseline/control: Agentless, SWE-Agent, SWE-Search, OpenHands, EvoCoder, SAGE
claims.selection_vs_test: k, N and bank-size chosen/analysed on the same benchmark; bank built from other instances of that benchmark
claims.allowed_conclusion: Higher single-run Pass@1 than the listed scaffolds; Claude margin (+2.2, i.e. 11 issues) is within plausible run noise; SOTA comparison relies on numbers of unstated provenance.

claims.text: Retained experience contributes independently of the dual-agent design (comprehension, modification, extraction, reranking each matter).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Experience adds about +4.2 pt over the no-experience configuration in one DeepSeek run; raw golden-patch demonstrations are worse than none.
Per-instance online overhead small; bank-construction cost not included.
Cross-repo claim not isolated: same-repo earlier experiences remain eligible and no per-repo or cross-repo-only analysis is given.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Experience distilled offline from earlier benchmark trajectories (with repo/time exclusion) and retrieved at k=1 improved single-run SWE-Bench Verified Pass@1 by about 4.2 points over a no-experience configuration of the same scaffold with DeepSeek-V3; the larger headline gain also includes the dual-agent redesign, and the Claude margin over SWE-Search is small.

G.reason: Concrete, sourced limitation (stateless exploration) with the experience-agent neighbors named and two compared; residual vs SAGE/EvoCoder argued qualitatively; part of the novelty is SE specialization (F2 partial).

M.reason: Two-facet abstraction, rerank and instruction-rewriting each have an explicit rationale and a tested alternative (raw demos, similarity-only, k sweep); reason experience helps is argued by one case study, applicability assumptions untested.

X.reason: Write, retrieve, rewrite chain is reconstructable with prompts, but no gate on admission, no update/forgetting/versioning/rollback, bank frozen and built once from baseline trajectories; 'continuous learning' is not implemented as a loop; applicability check absent by authors' admission.

E.measurement.reason: SWE-Bench Verified with test-validated resolution is a credible validator; base-model contamination conceded and baseline numbers of mixed provenance prevent a 4.

E.causality.reason: Store-off (k=0) within the full scaffold, alternative abstraction (raw golden-patch demos), rerank-off and role-split ablations isolate the experience effect; ablations run on DeepSeek only, no random/irrelevant-experience control, headline vs SWE-Search confounded with dual-agent, margins small for the single-run noise.

E.holdout.reason: Documented repo/time exclusion keeps the target out of its own bank, but the bank comes from the evaluation benchmark, same-repo earlier items allowed, k and bank size tuned on the test benchmark, no fresh or cross-language set, base-model overlap unverifiable.

E.statistics.reason: n=500 stated but single run, no seeds or intervals; no-experience baseline reported as both 37.8 and 37.2; non-monotone k curve and 131 always-solved issues indicate noise comparable to some margins (frozen ladder level 1).

E.cost.reason: Online tokens, API cost and wall time versus SWE-Search reported, but cost of collecting trajectories and extracting experiences for the bank is excluded, Claude cost not reported, no compute-matched baseline.
